transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO), Ravi (Lead ML Eng), Elena (Head Product)

Summary:
Seashell Digital is evaluating Redwood for a fast PLG onramp (time-to-first-call) with an eventual private deployment requirement for regulated media workloads. They're leaning toward starting hosted/self-serve to move quickly but need answers on security, cost projections, and how we run benchmarks that reflect their token distribution and KV cache usage.

Topics: quickstart credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC2/KMS, benchmark plan, pilot acceptance criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and Priya our solutions engineer is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good thanks, yes thanks for fitting us in. We only have about 45 minutes so want to be efficient.
[00:12] Jordan: Totally, we'll aim for a quick run and some concrete next steps. Quick round robin — who all is here?
[00:18] Maya: Maya — CTO.
[00:20] Ravi: Ravi, lead ML eng.
[00:22] Elena: Elena, product.
[00:24] Priya: Priya Nair, solutions eng at Redwood.
[00:26] Jordan: Cool. So high level — you flagged two things in the form: short path to first request with credits and then a longer private/VPC path for production. Is that right, Maya?
[00:36] Maya: Correct. We want to demo a user-facing summarization feature in our mobile app in a 6 week sprint. Ideally host the prototype on Redwood hosted API so product can iterate, then later move to a VPC/private deployment for compliance.
[00:47] Jordan: Great. On credits — we do free onboarding credits for PLG signups, and for potential pilots we can extend a hosted pilot credit grant. Time-to-first-token for typical teams is under an hour for a dev to make the first call. With our quickstart repo and SDKs you can usually be generating in < 30 minutes.
[01:05] Ravi: Couple of questions — what are the default rate limits on hosted? And if we need a stable P95 latency for demos, how do we guarantee that without a dedicated pool?
[01:16] Priya: Good Q. Hosted has conservative per-account rate limits by default but we can temporarily raise them for pilots. For predictable latency we recommend either dedicated or shaping your requests plus using our smaller model variants. Also automatic prefix caching and KV cache can reduce tail latency for repeated contexts.
[01:32] Elena: Can you explain the KV cache bit — will that help our use case where users request summaries repeatedly on similar docs?
[01:38] Priya: Yes — KV cache is stored at the runtime layer to avoid re-decoding tokens from the early prompt so repeated similar inputs get big wins. There's a cache hit rate tradeoff depending on prompt variability — we can simulate with your sample prompts in the benchmark.
[01:51] Maya: On the private side — we have auditors who insist on customer-managed keys and dedicated networking. Does Redwood Private support bring-your-own-KMS and VPC peering?
[02:02] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports BYOK through our KMS integrations and we can deploy the control plane into your VPC or on-prem bundle depending on the deal. There are slight differences in telemetry retention and console access but we document that. We'll include the security whitepaper.
[02:18] Ravi: Any certs we should know about? SOC2? ISO?
[02:21] Jordan: We have SOC2 Type II. For ISO we partner with providers on request — we'll include the cert summary in the pack.
[02:29] Elena: Pricing — we need a rough estimate for a 3-month pilot: about 100k tokens/day with peak spikes up to 300 reqs/min during launch tests. How should we model cost?
[02:42] Priya: Two levers — model choice and batching. For hosted we price per-token for generation and for embeddings separately. If you target a smaller open variant and enable batching you'll reduce per-token latency/cost. We can produce a cost model once you share expected input/output token sizes.
[02:58] Jordan: If you want I'll put together a simple cost sheet showing hosted vs dedicated vs private for the pilot profile you just described.
[03:05] Maya: Yes please. Also, can you do a quick note on how rerouting works if we want fallback to cheaper model when high load?
[03:13] Priya: Sure — smart routing policies can route by latency budget, cost tier, or region. For example you can set a rule: prefer model-alpha but fall back to model-beta when load > X or latency > Y. That keeps the app online with graceful degradation.
[03:30] Ravi: For benchmark — we need to validate latency and hallucination/regression for our prompt set. Is there an eval harness you recommend?
[03:38] Priya: We have an evals repo and suggested prompts. For hallucination/regression, you can use our quality monitoring tied to prompt sets, and we can set regression alerts. For latency we'll run load tests with and without KV cache, with batching, and across sequence length tails.
[03:52] Elena: How invasive is Redwood SDK — our front-end is React Native. Can we call the API directly or is a microservice layer recommended?
[03:59] Jordan: Many customers call via a backend microservice to keep keys off the client. For prototypes people sometimes call directly from backendless setups with ephemeral keys but for production we recommend a proxy microservice with RBAC tokens.
[04:12] Maya: Security question — data retention. If we start hosted for prototype, will customer data be persisted by Redwood, and can we configure retention windows?
[04:21] Jordan: Hosted stores logs and telemetry. We have configurable retention and deletion options and an option to disable retention for requests if you need minimal persistence. For Private you control logs entirely. We'll include the retention matrix in the docs.
[04:35] Ravi: Can you walk through the typical pilot acceptance criteria? For us it's: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for median prompt, error rate < 0.5%, and quality pass rate on our prompt tests > 92% relative to baseline.
[04:50] Priya: That sounds reasonable. For the hosted pilot we can agree on target KPIs, run the baseline and the regression eval. We can also include canary rollouts and auto-fallback during the pilot.
[05:04] Elena: One more — do you support pre-compiled kernels or quantized variants for cheaper inference? We care about cost.
[05:12] Priya: Yes, our runtime supports quantized variants and selects kernels per hardware; we also recommend mixed-precision on some footprints. For hosted we manage that. For Private we give tooling and recommendations.
[05:24] Maya: Great. Ok let's talk logistics — we want to run a 2-week hosted pilot first and then discuss Dedicated capacity for production. Timeline: start pilot within 2 weeks if we can. Is that feasible?
[05:35] Jordan: Totally feasible. Steps I'd propose: you send sample payloads and expected traffic curve, we run a benchmark and share results, we provision a short-term pilot credit and adjust rate limits, then you validate app UX and KPIs.
[05:48] Ravi: For the benchmarks — we need reproducible tests. Priya, could you include setup instructions and the harness?
[05:55] Priya: I'll package a script that can run locally or in your cloud; it will toggle KV cache and batching. Also include sample environment variables for hosted creds and a Docker image.
[06:08] Elena: Who owns the pilot environment? If we start hosted pilot and later move to Private, will there be data migration concerns?
[06:15] Jordan: Migration is mostly about model artifacts and data policies. We'll provide export hooks and an onboarding checklist for moving from hosted to private. It's not seamless zero-downtime but it's straightforward for the typical workloads we've seen.
[06:30] Maya: Ok good. Anything else on compliance?
[06:34] Jordan: We'll include SSO/SAML guidance, RBAC, and audit log details in the security pack.
[06:40] Ravi: One oddball — our infra team asks whether Redwood ever exposes KV cache contents to customers.
[06:46] Priya: KV cache is not visible as a raw dump in hosted; for Private you can configure logging/exposure per your policies. We'll note that in the docs.
[06:57] Maya: Sounds good. Let's capture the actions.

Action recap (spoken):
[07:05] Jordan: Next steps recap — I'll send security + pricing, Priya will prepare the harness, Ravi will share payloads. We'll schedule the benchmarking window after we get the samples.

Closing notes / misc chatter:
[07:20] Elena: Quick question — is there a Slack channel or direct point for pilot escalation?
[07:24] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide a dedicated Slack channel for the pilot and an on-call SE contact.
[07:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[07:33] Jordan: Thanks team — we'll follow up with the pack by Friday.

End of transcript.
